mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕体育运动展开，涵盖奥运精神与传奇运动员（Reading）、体育习语融入日常语言（Extended reading）和正确看待输赢（Integrated skills）三个子话题——体育是高考应用文'活动/人物'类的高频场景，也是雅思教育与社会类议论文的经典命题。

subTopics.title: 奥运精神与传奇运动员
subTopics.desc: 课文核心：顾拜旦 brought the Olympics back to life；运动员 motivated by the Olympic motto 'Faster, Higher, Stronger'，devoted themselves to achieving sporting excellence and pushing the boundaries of human achievement。

prompts.task: 你校将举办体育节开幕式，你受邀作为学生代表用英文发言，谈谈'我最敬佩的运动员'。请写一篇发言稿，内容包括：1. 该运动员的事迹；2. 你敬佩的原因；3. 对同学们的号召。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Good morning, everyone. It is a great honour to speak at our sports festival.

The athlete I admire most is a boxing champion who came to public attention during the 1960 Rome Olympics, when he won a gold medal for his country, demonstrating great talent and personality in the process. Motivated by the Olympic motto "Faster, Higher, Stronger", he devoted himself to achieving sporting excellence and pushing the boundaries of human achievement.

What touches me most is not the medals, but the spirit of solidarity and fair play behind them. True athletes test their ability against each other in the hope of bringing out the best in everyone.

Let's carry this spirit into our studies and lives. Thank you!
vocabHints: push the boundaries of human achievement
in the spirit of solidarity and fair play
test their ability against each other

prompts.task: Some people think that hosting international sporting events such as the Olympic Games brings great benefits to a country, while others believe it is an expensive waste of money. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Whenever a city bids for the Olympic Games, the same debate ignites: supporters promise national renewal, while opponents see a festival of waste. Having weighed both positions, I believe hosting can be genuinely worthwhile, but only for countries that already possess most of the required infrastructure.

The case for hosting rests on more than money. A successful Games raises a country's international profile, attracts tourists for years afterwards, and accelerates investment in transport, housing and sports facilities that residents continue to use long after the athletes leave. The intangible benefits matter too: shared national pride, thousands of volunteers gaining organisational skills, and children inspired to take up sport after watching competition at the highest level.

Sceptics, however, point to a long record of financial disaster. Stadiums built for a fortnight of competition often decay into expensive ruins; budgets are routinely exceeded several times over; and the billions spent might have funded hospitals or schools instead. In developing countries especially, the opportunity cost of prestige projects can be painful, and the promised tourism boom frequently fails to materialise once the closing ceremony ends.

In my opinion, the deciding factor is preparation, not principle. Cities that reuse existing venues and integrate the Games into long-term urban plans convert a short event into lasting public assets; cities that build from nothing for the sake of spectacle almost guarantee regret. Hosting the Olympics is therefore neither a blessing nor a curse in itself: it is an amplifier, magnifying the wisdom or the vanity of the government that stages it.

subTopics.title: 突破极限
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：my limits were being tested like never before、there is no limit to、within one's limits——真正的成长，往往发生在极限被一次次试探的时刻。

prompts.task: 你校英文报以 "Beyond My Limits" 为题征稿。请你写一篇短文，讲述一次突破自我极限的经历，内容包括：1. 事情经过；2. 你的收获。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Last term I signed up for the school's 10-kilometre run, though I had never run more than three.

On race day, I ran relaxed and confident at first, but by the eighth kilometre my limits were being tested like never before. My legs burned and a voice inside kept telling me to stop. Instead of giving up, I told myself that there is no limit to what I could try, and pushed on one step at a time.

I did not win, but I crossed the line — and that was enough. I learned that our limits are often further away than they feel. Sometimes we only discover how strong we are when we refuse to quit.
vocabHints: my limits were being tested like never before
a voice inside kept telling me to stop
pushed on one step at a time

prompts.task: Some people believe that the main purpose of sport is to win, while others think that taking part and improving oneself matters more than winning. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Every competition eventually raises the same question: does sport exist to produce winners, or to let people take part and grow? Some prize victory above all; others insist that participation and self-improvement matter more. In my view both have their place, but for the vast majority of people the value of sport lies in taking part rather than in winning.

The winning-first view has genuine merit, especially at the top. Elite sport is built on the pursuit of victory; without the drive to win, records would never fall and standards would stagnate. Competition pushes athletes to test their limits like never before, and the discipline this demands can be admirable in itself. For professionals, winning is quite reasonably the point.

Yet for almost everyone else, this emphasis is misplaced. Most people who play sport will never be champions, and if winning were all that mattered, they would have little reason to continue. What they gain instead is real and lasting: fitness, friendship, teamwork and the steady satisfaction of improving against their own past performance. A child who finishes last but returns each week learns persistence no trophy could teach, whereas an obsession with winning can breed cheating, anxiety and early burnout.

The healthiest attitude, therefore, depends on context. At the elite level winning rightly drives excellence, but in schools and ordinary life participation and personal progress should come first.

In conclusion, while the desire to win has its proper place in professional sport, for most people sport is most valuable as a source of health, connection and self-improvement — and it is these, not medals, that last a lifetime.

subTopics.title: 正确看待输赢
subTopics.desc: 综合技能板块核心：winning has the victor walking on air... while the loser is left with a bitter taste；关键在 keep everything in perspective——at any sporting event, you face two opponents。

prompts.task: 你的英国朋友 Chris 在网球决赛中失利，情绪低落。请你用英文给他写一封信，内容包括：1. 表达安慰；2. 谈谈你对输赢的看法；3. 提出鼓励和建议。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Chris,

I'm sorry to hear that you lost the final of the tennis tournament and have been feeling down these days. Please don't be too hard on yourself.

We all know what it is like to want to win, and most of us know what it is like to lose. More often than not, winning has the victor walking on air, while the loser is left with a bitter taste. But remember: at any sporting event, you face two opponents — the other player and yourself. By finishing the match bravely, you have already beaten the second one, so try to keep everything in perspective.

I believe your consistent good performance will pay off next season. Whenever you need a training partner, don't hesitate to call me.

Yours,
Li Hua
vocabHints: what it is like to lose
be left with a bitter taste

prompts.task: Some people think that competitive sports teach children to win at all costs, while others believe such sports teach children valuable life lessons. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Whether competitive sport shapes children for better or worse divides parents and educators. Some fear it trains the young to pursue victory at any price; others regard the sports field as one of life's best classrooms. I side mainly with the second group, provided adults manage the competition sensibly.

Those who worry about competition have real cases to cite. When trophies become the only measure of success, children may cheat, bully weaker teammates or burn out physically before adolescence. Pushy parents shouting from the sidelines can turn a game into a source of dread, and the lesson absorbed is that losing equals worthlessness — a belief that damages mental health long after childhood ends.

Yet these are failures of supervision, not of sport itself. Properly guided competition teaches lessons that classrooms struggle to deliver: how to prepare seriously, how to cooperate with teammates of different abilities, how to win with grace and, above all, how to lose, recover and try again. A child who learns to shake an opponent's hand after defeat is rehearsing resilience for examinations, job interviews and every later setback. Team sports also anchor friendships and physical health at an age when screens compete for every free hour.

In conclusion, competitive sport is a powerful instrument whose effect depends on the hands that hold it. Stripped of perspective it can indeed breed a win-at-all-costs mentality, but under sensible coaching it builds discipline, fairness and emotional strength. Rather than shielding children from competition, we should teach them to compete honourably — a skill they will need for the rest of their lives.

subTopics.title: 体育融入日常语言
subTopics.desc: 拓展阅读核心：Since sport is an inseparable part of day-to-day life, there are lots of sports idioms that have found their way into everyday language——足球、棒球等运动为英语贡献了大量习语。

prompts.task: 你校英语角将举办'趣味英语'分享会，你准备以体育习语为主题发言。请写一篇发言稿，内容包括：1. 体育习语进入日常语言的现象；2. 举例说明一两个习语的来源和用法；3. 学习建议。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Hello, everyone! Welcome to today's English corner. My topic is sports idioms.

Since sport is an inseparable part of day-to-day life, lots of sports idioms have found their way into everyday language. Take football. In a match, players try to kick or head the ball into the opposing team's goal, so English borrows many vivid expressions from the pitch. Baseball gives us another example: a batter is out if he makes three unsuccessful attempts to hit the ball, which is why a failed attempt in life is often called a "strike". And if someone's cooking is far better than mine, I simply admit I am not in her league.

Idioms like these make our English vivid and natural. Why not collect a few and try them out this week?
vocabHints: an inseparable part of day-to-day life
find one's way into everyday language

prompts.task: Some people believe that to learn a foreign language well, it is necessary to understand the culture of the countries where it is spoken. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
It is widely claimed that mastering a foreign language demands more than memorising vocabulary and grammar: learners must also understand the culture in which the language lives. I agree almost entirely with this view, since language and culture are woven together at every level of real communication.

The strongest evidence lies in everyday expressions. Idioms, jokes, politeness formulas and even sporting metaphors carry meanings that no dictionary entry fully explains; a learner who translates them word by word often ends up puzzled or, worse, unintentionally rude. Knowing when to be direct, how to refuse an offer gracefully, or which topics are sensitive at a dinner table is cultural knowledge, yet it determines whether a grammatically perfect sentence succeeds or fails. Business negotiators and exchange students alike discover that fluency without cultural awareness produces misunderstanding faster than silence does.

Admittedly, the necessary depth of cultural study depends on the learner's purpose. A scientist reading technical papers in English needs terminology far more than table manners, and global English today is spoken mostly between non-native speakers, which dilutes the influence of any single national culture. Nevertheless, even these cases involve culture in a broader sense: the conventions of academic writing differ sharply between countries, and international communication has developed customs of its own that still must be learned.

In conclusion, while the required dose of cultural understanding varies with one's goals, a language detached from its culture remains a code rather than a means of genuine connection. Learners who explore films, customs and social habits alongside grammar communicate more accurately — and enjoy the journey far more.
